status_summary: On 2025-11-17 the Under Secretary for Research and Engineering announced six critical technology areas: applied artificial intelligence, biomanufacturing, contested logistics technologies, quantum and battlefield information dominance, scaled directed energy, and scaled hypersonics. The official release names the six areas but does not say they replace an earlier list, mention the number 14, address funding for areas left off, or name a governing memo. AIP and Breaking Defense report that the six replace the 14 areas of the 2023 list, with FutureG, integrated sensing and cyber, and quantum folded into the quantum and battlefield information dominance area and others, including microelectronics and renewable energy generation and storage, dropped. Breaking Defense quotes the office as saying it will keep investing in technologies outside the list, while AIP quotes the Under Secretary as saying items off the list will not have effort and budget behind them. DefenseScoop reported on 2026-01-30 that the office had named a lead official for each of the six areas and that a detailed plan for the planned technology sprints had not yet been released. No later change to the list was found.

timeline.event: Under Secretary for Research and Engineering announces six critical technology areas: applied artificial intelligence, biomanufacturing, contested logistics, quantum and battlefield information dominance, scaled directed energy and scaled hypersonics. AIP reports the list of 14 was cut to six and details which areas were merged or dropped.

title: Cut DOD critical technology areas from 14 to a smaller set
uncertainties: The official release on war.gov was opened by direct fetch by the researcher and again by the independent reviewer (the original defense.gov address returned not found, and a no-slug war.gov address was reported blocked in a browser retrieval supplied to the project). It lists the six areas and shows no date, no mention of a prior list or the number 14, no funding language and no memo. The replacement of the 14 therefore rests on AIP and Breaking Defense; the stage is implemented because the six-area list is operative as an announced priority set; progress is 90 because the numerical reduction is reported consistently by two trade sources and the official release's silence on the old list is a gap in the evidence rather than a sign of less implementation, which is reflected in confidence instead. The two articles differ on whether work outside the six will still be funded. The release date of 2025-11-17 comes from a mirror and press coverage, not the official page. Stage is not completed because the list is an internal priority set that can be revised without notice and the effect on budgets was not checked. The Breaking Defense article carries no date in the text read. A third trade report (DefenseScoop, 2025-08-27) says the list had grown to 14 under the prior administration and that the Under Secretary planned to cut it, and DefenseScoop on 2026-01-30 describes the cut from 14 to six, which adds a further press source but no official statement of the number 14. The FY2027 RDT&E R-1 budget exhibit (comptroller site, April 2026) was opened and did not mention the six areas by name, so budget realignment remains unverified. No memo or later list change was found in searches of trade press. The naming of a lead official for each of the six areas is reported by DefenseScoop in an article dated 2026-01-30, which says the leads were announced on social media on a Thursday evening without giving a date; because no source states the date of the announcement, it is kept here rather than as a timeline event (the likely date is 2026-01-29, inferred and not confirmed).
